title: Comparative In Vitro ADME Assessment and Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic (PBPK) Modeling of Andrographolide and Its Tert-Butyldiphenylsilyl (TBDPS)-Protected Analogue
content: Andrographolide, has been reported to have many biological activities such as anti-inflammatory, anticancer, antiviral, and immunomodulatory activities. However, its therapeutic potential is limited by poor oral bioavailability of around 2.67%, which may be due to rapid hepatic and intestinal metabolism. In this study, a tert-butyldiphenylsilyl (TBDPS) analog of andrographolide, modified at the C-19 position with a C16H19Si group to protect the hydroxyl functionality from enzymatic oxidation, was evaluated. In vitro ADME characterization compared lipophilicity, plasma protein binding, and stability for andrographolide and its TBDPS analogue. PBPK modeling was used to compare their pharmacokinetic behavior. Compared to the parent compound, the TBDPS analog exhibited greater lipophilicity, higher plasma protein binding, improved plasma stability, and reduced hepatic microsomal clearance. The PBPK simulation demonstrated slower metabolic clearance of the TBDPS analog, though it attained a lower maximal concentration than the parent molecule. These results suggest TBDPS modification improves andrographolide stability and pharmacokinetic properties. However, the PBPK results showed that the analog may still have limitations, especially in plasma exposure and elimination, so further formulation and in vivo exposure studies are needed.
